title: Wizard generate step intermittently unreliable
description: Mitigated by the Tailwind CSS migration: the wizard's document generation now authors Tailwind classes inline during structure generation instead of a separate CSS-rules-writing phase, and the second AI call only sets styles.variables (brand palette) instead of a full CSS-rules object - much shorter total output, lower truncation/omission risk. Verified: the editor-transform happy-path test (which hits the real configured AI_PROVIDER, not a mock) went from failing on live model runs before the prompt rewrite to 4/4 passes after. Residual variance remains possible if the live model picks Tailwind syntax outside the allowlist's scope (e.g. arbitrary-value shadow colors) - that surfaces as a normal invalid_operations rejection, same as any other allowlist miss, not a truncation failure.

The equivalent ongoing-maintenance item going forward is Tailwind class allowlist coverage, tracked implicitly via apps/ai_assistant/tailwind_classes.py.

Explicitly completed before a third consumer because the shared API is isolated and covered by a Node regression.

title: Image upload for the wizard
description: POST /api/user-templates/wizard-images/ (WizardImageUploadView) - Pillow re-encodes every upload from scratch (format/size validated, downscaled to 1600px long edge, always re-saved as JPEG, stripping EXIF), owner-scoped UploadedAsset model, per-user upload cap. Registered in state.assets, but never AI-authored: wizard_service.py builds assets server-side from exactly what the client already uploaded, and the model only picks a URL from that list to put in . document_validation.py validates the shape regardless (check_asset_entry, url must be under /media/). Minimal wizard UI (file input + thumbnail strip) wired into the existing question-form step.

title: styles.rules gained @media support
description: editor-core.js's buildCss() already rendered styles.mediaQueries (dead code, never populated) and it was completely unvalidated on the Python side - a latent CSS-injection gap. Fixed both at once: document_validation.py now validates styles.mediaQueries (allowlisted query string via check_css_media_query, nested rules reuse the same selector/declarations checks); the wizard styles prompt now tells the AI it can use it. Scope: only covers wizard full-document generation, not the editor's incremental AI-transform.

title: Structured request logging/metrics for AI usage and error rates

Bonus: the wizard views had the same uncaught-exception gap as the transform 500 fix - added the same except Exception catch-all there too.

Added the same revision-retention cap (20) to apps/projects/views.py that UserTemplate already has.

title: Tailwind CSS migration
description: Styling moved from a custom JSON DSL (styles.rules: AI/editor-authored {selector, declarations} objects validated against CSS_PROPERTY_ALLOWLIST) to Tailwind utility classes on attributes.class, validated against a finite allowlist (tailwind_classes.py: is_allowed_tailwind_class/check_class_list, wired into operations.py's set_attribute and sanitize.py's check_attributes). New Tailwind v4 CLI build pipeline (pnpm run build:css): a management command materializes the class allowlist into a safelist sentinel file that is Tailwind's ONLY content source (tailwind-input.css uses source(none) plus explicit @source), since AI-chosen classes never appear in any file Tailwind could otherwise scan, and because Tailwind's default whole-project auto-scan was verified to compile any Tailwind-shaped string found anywhere (including test fixtures). Wizard document generation now authors classes inline during structure generation; the second AI call only sets the brand-color palette. The editor's per-element quick-style panel now toggles Tailwind classes instead of writing an inline style="" attribute (a second, previously undocumented styling mechanism this consolidated away). styles.rules/mediaQueries/keyframes remain in the schema and keep rendering for backward compatibility with every pre-migration Template/UserTemplate/Project row - verified end-to-end with a hand-seeded legacy document (still renders its old CSS, its gallery thumbnail, and remains editable). Docker/CI/local setup updated to build the CSS (Node 20 required - Debian bookworm's apt nodejs is too old for Tailwind v4).

title: Public template publishing + storefront (products, Stripe checkout, digital downloads)
description: UserTemplate gains is_published/public_slug (stable once set); new GET /t/<slug>/ (PublicTemplateView) renders a full standalone document server-side (apps/editor/rendering.py's public_page_html) for anonymous visitors, no editor scripts, 404 identically for nonexistent and unpublished. New apps/storefront app: Product (price_cents, optional image, optional digital_file for downloadables, validated by real magic-byte sniffing not extension/Content-Type) and Order (the permanent purchase record, created ONLY by a signature-verified Stripe webhook, never the checkout-redirect view). PaymentProvider abstraction (FakePaymentProvider/StripePaymentProvider) mirrors the existing AIProvider/FakeAIProvider swappable pattern - PAYMENT_PROVIDER defaults to fake, tests never touch the real Stripe API. Checkout always re-reads price from the DB, never trusts the client. Digital downloads are served through a token-gated view (never a static /media/ URL) with a download-count cap; the success page explicitly handles the webhook-vs-redirect race condition via a direct provider session lookup fallback instead of assuming the Order already exists. Editor UI: Publicar/Despublicar toggle in the save modal, a Productos management page (/productos/), and an Insertar producto control that adds a real product card with a working Comprar form to the page. Verified end-to-end with real Playwright runs: publish+view+unpublish, create a product with an image and PDF (owner-scoped), insert a product card, and the full anonymous checkout -> pending -> simulated webhook -> paid flow. Real Stripe test-mode keys were not available in this environment - the full real-Stripe-hosted-checkout-page round trip was not run; only the FakePaymentProvider path was verified live.

title: Fix AI-rejected max-w-4xl class and enable YouTube/Vimeo iframe embeds
description: A user-reported screenshot of the AI panel rejecting an instruction ("agrega este video de YouTube") with a generic "cambios no válidos" error had two independent real causes, both found via live server-log reproduction rather than guessing from the screenshot. (1) tailwind_classes.py's max-w utility family only allowed the numeric SIZING_SCALE, missing Tailwind's separate named container-width scale (max-w-4xl, prose, none, etc.) - added MAX_WIDTH_NAMED_SCALE, scoped to max-w only (w/min-w/h/min-h/max-h unaffected). (2) iframe was fully forbidden in sanitize.py's FORBIDDEN_TAGS, silently blocking a legitimate, common request - replaced with a tag-specific src-prefix allowlist (youtube.com/embed, youtube-nocookie.com/embed, player.vimeo.com/video) so arbitrary iframe src is still rejected (clickjacking/phishing risk on now-public template pages) but real video embeds work. AI system prompt updated to convert watch URLs to embed URLs and use aspect-video instead of an arbitrary pb-[56.25%] hack. Verified end-to-end by re-running the exact original failing instruction against a live server and confirming a successful add_node operation with a working iframe.

title: Route ""Insertar producto"" through the AI instead of a hardcoded unstyled node

Rather than hand-writing Tailwind classes into the deterministic template, routed the insert through the existing AI transform pipeline: EditorTransformView now populates EditorContext.available_products server-side from the requesting user's OWN active products (id/name/price_cents/image_url) - never client-supplied, so the model can't reference a product it doesn't own or invent an id. The SYSTEM_PROMPT gained an exact card-shape spec (data-product-id/data-buy-form/action) the model fills with real Tailwind classes. editor-ai.js exposes a new EditorAI.requestInstruction(text) entry point (opens the drawer, forces global_mode, sends the instruction) that editor-core.js's insertProductButton now calls instead of pushing a hardcoded node. User explicitly chose this over a quick deterministic-Tailwind fix after being shown the tradeoff (latency/cost/variability vs instant/free/consistent).

title: Fix CSRF 403 on checkout/webhook for logged-in sessions
description: CheckoutView and StripeWebhookView are @csrf_exempt + AllowAny, but DRF's default SessionAuthentication runs its own CSRF check independent of that decorator whenever it successfully authenticates a request via session cookie - a logged-in visitor (e.g. the template owner testing their own Comprar button, as reported via screenshot showing 'CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing.' on /comprar/6/) got a 403 despite the view being explicitly csrf_exempt. Fixed with authentication_classes = [] on both views (no reason to authenticate a fully public/AllowAny request at all). Existing tests never caught this because the api/anon_api fixtures use force_authenticate, which bypasses DRF's real auth+CSRF pipeline entirely - added a regression test using a real client.login() session with enforce_csrf_checks=True, verified it 403s without the fix and 302s with it.

title: Fix fake-provider checkout stuck forever on Procesando tu pago
description: With PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake (default, no Stripe keys configured), FakePaymentProvider marked a session paid instantly but nothing ever created the Order row - that only happens in StripeWebhookView.post, and there is no real Stripe server in dev/test to ever deliver that webhook. Reproduced live: a real logged-in browser session got permanently stuck on 'Procesando tu pago... Todavia estamos confirmando tu pago' right after the checkout CSRF fix (row 46) unblocked the redirect itself. Fixed by extracting the webhook's order-creation logic into a shared _record_order_for_session() and having CheckoutView call it directly right after session creation, ONLY when the provider is FakePaymentProvider - real Stripe checkouts are untouched, still require the actual signed webhook.

title: UI/UX: consolidate 3 drifted design-token sets into one shared stylesheet
description: Extracted the canonical palette, typography, radius, and shadow variables into static/shared/tokens.css, linked it across server-rendered surfaces, and verified it structurally and in a real browser.

title: Multi-gateway checkout (Stripe/Mercado Pago/PayPal/Braintree/Wompi/PayU/ePayco/Bold)
description: Executed per PAYMENTS.md (deleted after this close-out - see openspec/specs/storefront/spec.md for the permanent behavioral contract, CHANGELOG.md for the shipped-feature record). Buyer picks gateway at checkout; PaymentGatewayConfig is owner-scoped and Fernet-encrypted at rest (apps/storefront/crypto.py); each gateway has real+Fake* provider pair behind GATEWAY_REGISTRY (apps/storefront/payments.py); Order gained a gateway field, uniqueness scoped per (gateway, gateway_session_id); GatewayWebhookView tries every enabled seller's credentials for a gateway until one verifies the signature. New /config/ page + /api/payment-gateway-configs/ (credentials write-only, never returned). AI product-card prompt now emits one buy-form per available_gateways entry. Verified end-to-end via a real browser click-through: /config toggle -> publish page -> click real Comprar button -> gracias page, for the Stripe fake-provider path. Confidence/verification depth varies sharply by gateway (see openspec/specs/storefront/spec.md and learnings.jsonl id 2026-07-23-15): Stripe/Mercado Pago/Wompi/PayU/ePayco have local HMAC/checksum signature tests (accept+reject); PayPal/Braintree tested with mocked network/SDK calls; Bold's real webhook spec was never confirmable (JS-rendered docs returned no usable content) so BoldPaymentProvider.parse_webhook_event always raises rather than pretend to verify something unconfirmed - do not treat Bold as production-ready without first getting its real docs.

title: Fix legacy /comprar/<id>/ (no gateway) 404 on already-published pages
description: The multi-gateway checkout migration (row 49) changed /comprar/<id>/ to /comprar/<id>/<gateway>/, but a UserTemplate's buy-form action is a literal value baked into stored state JSON at insert time - never regenerated when the URL pattern changes. An already-published page's Comprar button 404'd for real (reproduced live via screenshot: /comprar/6/). Fixed with a legacy URL (checkout-legacy, same CheckoutView, gateway=None) falling back to the seller's first enabled PaymentGatewayConfig (deterministic order) - still 404s if the seller has enabled nothing at all via /config.

title: Deliver product for free (tracked $0 Order) when seller has no gateway enabled
description: Explicit user decision: rather than 404 (or an untracked silent giveaway) when a seller has zero PaymentGatewayConfig rows enabled, CheckoutView now delivers the product/downloadable directly AND creates a real, permanent Order (gateway=Order.Gateway.NONE, amount_cents=0, status=PAID) - auditable exactly like any real purchase. SuccessView accepts gateway=none. Verified end-to-end via a real browser click on a published page's Comprar button with no gateway configured at all.

Verified with 251 PostgreSQL pytest tests, Node checks, Tailwind build, and 15 Playwright tests at desktop and 320px; synchronized OpenSpec and project records afterward.
